title: Bidirectional A* finds routes from both ends!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* visualize how two heuristic-guided searches meet on a real street-map grid. You’ll see fewer explored nodes and faster convergence compared to one-way routing.
ig_caption:
🧭✨ Route-finding, but make it *smarter*.

In this visualization, **Bidirectional A*** runs two A* searches at the same time—one from the start and one from the goal—using a heuristic to guide exploration. When the forward and backward frontiers collide, the algorithm stitches the optimal path together. 🧩⚡

On a **real road network** (street-map graph built from intersections as nodes and roads as edges), this reduces wasted travel through the search space: instead of pushing from one direction until it “happens to reach” the goal, we narrow the gap from both sides. 📍📍

Want a deeper breakdown? Drop a 🚦 in the comments and I’ll explain the frontier meeting condition + how the heuristic affects node expansions.

👉 Follow for more real-map algorithm visualizations and tag a friend who loves pathfinding! 🧠💻
fb_caption:
Ever wondered how maps find the *fastest* route so quickly? 🌍

This reel visualizes **Bidirectional A***: two heuristic-guided searches expand from the start and the goal simultaneously on a graph made from real street intersections and roads. When the searches meet, the path is reconstructed—often with fewer explored nodes than traditional one-direction graph search.

Like, share, and comment what you want to see next: Dijkstra, A*, or D* Lite? 🚀

Perfect for: pathfinding visualization, AI search algorithms, graph theory, and coding education.
